questions.question: What is the primary raw material used to produce most traditional plastic food packaging?
options: Fossil fuels
Biomass
Recycled paper
Geothermal energy

questions.question: Why is plastic waste in oceans and landfills considered a significant environmental hazard?
options: It degrades too quickly, releasing toxic gases
It takes a very long time to degrade and can harm wildlife
It absorbs solar radiation and heats the water directly
It prevents marine plants from performing cellular respiration

questions.question: What makes biodegradable bioplastics a more sustainable alternative to traditional plastics for packaging?
options: They are manufactured using coal and natural gas
They are made from renewable resources and can break down naturally
They never decompose, allowing them to be reused indefinitely
They are completely impermeable to greenhouse gases

questions.question: Which of the following is a primary benefit of using plastic packaging for food items?
options: It increases the nutritional value of the food
It helps prevent food spoilage and reduces food waste
It absorbs excess greenhouse gases from the air
It speeds up the ripening process of fruits

questions.question: What is one of the main human activities driving global deforestation?
options: Urban vertical farming
Converting forest land for agricultural use
Establishing national parks
Recreational hiking and camping

questions.question: What is a direct consequence of deforestation on forest-dwelling wildlife?
options: An increase in available nesting sites
Rapid adaptation to urban environments
Habitat loss for many different species
An expansion of their geographical range

questions.question: How does global warming directly threaten human food security?
options: It increases the rate of soil formation globally
It puts global food production at risk due to changing climates
It makes all crops grow significantly faster and larger
It eliminates the need for agricultural pests

questions.question: Why does the increase in extreme weather events due to climate change make farming more difficult?
options: It stabilizes seasonal temperatures year-round
It reduces the global demand for agricultural crops
It makes it much more challenging to reliably produce food
It increases the predictability of rainfall patterns

questions.question: What contributes to the carbon footprint of the food we eat?
options: Only the respiration of the crops during their growth
Greenhouse gas emissions from multiple stages of food production
The heat released when food is cooked at home
The amount of water absorbed by plant roots

questions.question: How does the clearing of forests disrupt the carbon cycle?
options: It stops plants from releasing oxygen during respiration
It increases the rate of nitrogen fixation in the soil
Less carbon dioxide is absorbed from the atmosphere for photosynthesis
It prevents decomposers from breaking down organic matter

questions.question: What role does carbon dioxide play when its concentration increases in the atmosphere?
options: It acts as a greenhouse gas, enhancing the greenhouse effect and driving climate change
It thins the atmosphere, allowing harmful cosmic rays to reach the surface
It cools the planet by reflecting all incoming sunlight back into space
It directly blocks plants from performing aerobic respiration

questions.question: Why does deforestation have a major impact on the water cycle?
options: It increases the total volume of water on the Earth's surface
Less water is absorbed by tree roots and transpired into the atmosphere
It stops all rainfall from occurring worldwide
It converts groundwater directly into water vapor

questions.question: How can deforestation lead to increased flooding and threaten our food supply?
options: By decreasing the amount of surface runoff on agricultural land
By causing more water to run off the land surface, increasing flooding
By permanently lowering the sea level near coastal farms
By drying up all natural rivers and streams instantly

questions.question: What is a major consequence of climate change altering the environmental conditions of a habitat?
options: Species instantly mutate to become perfectly adapted
Species may become less well adapted to live in their changing habitat
The habitat becomes completely immune to ecological disruptions
All native species automatically increase their reproduction rates

questions.question: How do some species survive when climate change alters their original habitat's conditions?
options: They stop requiring energy and enter permanent dormancy
They migrate to a new habitat with suitable conditions
They learn to photosynthesize to avoid searching for food
They merge with other species to form new hybrid organisms
